terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation (-iō): with ex or ab + ablative, or with the accusative of the danger escaped
terms.comment: With the accusative of what one escapes (mortem effugere), or with ex of the place. Also simply to avoid or shun.
Properly to come out (of the water, a building) or climb up; so, to get away safe (ē perīculō, Cic. Div. 2.13). It also means to turn out, end up.

terms.register: vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; in ōrātiōne Cicerōnis rāra
terms.comment: To run off, take to one’s heels; mostly in comedy (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: an escape; a way of escape
terms.comment: For “escape” as a noun, Latin more often says fuga, flight, or uses the verb.

terms.grammar: conjiciō with the reflexive and in pedēs
terms.register: vōx cōmica: Ter.; Plaut. sē in pedēs cōnferre

phrases.latin: tum vulpēcula ēvāsit puteō nīxa celsīs cornibus hircumque clausō līquit haerentem vadō
phrases.english: then the little fox got out of the well, climbing on his tall horns, and left the goat stuck in the shut-in water

phrases.latin: cervus nemorōsīs excitātus latibulīs, ut vēnātōrum effugeret īnstantem necem, caecō timōre proximam vīllam petit
phrases.english: a stag, roused from his woodland hiding-places, made blindly for the nearest farm to escape the hunters closing in
